description:
The TransactionSystemLayout type is doing two jobs that FDB keeps in separate structures, and the seam is already visible as a lie in the type system.

FDB has two records with different lifetimes and audiences:
- DBCoreState (fdbserver/include/fdbserver/DBCoreState.h:132) — DURABLE, in the coordinated state. Holds tLogs, oldTLogData, recoveryCount. This is what recovery LOCKS and WRITES, and what tells the next recovery where to recover FROM.
- ServerDBInfo (fdbserver/include/fdbserver/ServerDBInfo.actor.h:41) — TRANSIENT broadcast. Its own comment: 'This structure contains transient information which is broadcast to all workers for a database, permitting them to communicate with each other.' Holds interfaces (master, resolvers, distributor), logSystemConfig, recoveryState.

Bedrock ALREADY has this split in STORAGE, just not in the types:
- ClusterBootstrap (priv/schemas/cluster_bootstrap.fbs, lib/bedrock/system_keys/cluster_bootstrap.ex) is our DBCoreState: cluster_id, epoch, logs (id + shard_tags + otp_ref), coordinators. Persisted to object storage, loaded by the coordinator at cold start. No pids.
- TransactionSystemLayout is our ServerDBInfo: epoch, sequencer, proxies, resolvers, logs — pids, rebuilt per recovery, broadcast.

THE LIE: coordinator/server.ex's build_old_tsl_from_bootstrap returns %{logs: logs} — one field — typed as TransactionSystemLayout.t(), which declares epoch, sequencer, proxies, resolvers AND logs as required(). Its own comment admits it: 'Recovery only uses the logs field to determine which logs to copy from.' Consumers are defensive because they know the value is partial: extract_old_system_services does Map.get(old_layout, :logs, %{}) (locking_phase.ex:154), and fresh_cluster?/1 matches %{logs: logs} because that is the only field really present (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:77-79).

CHANGE: introduce a CoreState type for the durable record and stop pretending it is a TSL.
- CoreState: epoch, logs (ids + shard_tags + locations). Backed by the ClusterBootstrap schema that already stores exactly these facts. This is the type recovery consumes as its prior state.
- TransactionSystemLayout: unchanged in content, but only ever the per-recovery broadcast — never persisted, never synthesized partially. Its existing docstring rule ('Nothing O(workers) may ever be added to this broadcast') stays and finally has a structural counterpart: things that must SURVIVE go in CoreState, things that must be REACHED go in the TSL.

MECHANICAL FALLOUT:
- Director.State / Director.Server / Recovery context: old_transaction_system_layout becomes prior_core_state, typed honestly (CoreState.t() | nil).
- locking_phase.ex extract_old_system_services: Map.get(old_layout, :logs, %{}) becomes plain field access.
- materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex fresh_cluster?/1 becomes 'no prior core state' rather than 'a TSL whose logs happen to be empty' — same behavior, honest predicate.
- coordinator/server.ex build_old_tsl_from_bootstrap becomes build_core_state_from_bootstrap and stops fabricating a TSL shape.

NOT IN SCOPE: adding fields to CoreState (bedrock-q67.21.12 adds the tag-0 members). This ticket is purely making the existing split visible in the types.

PREREQUISITE: bedrock-q67.21.10 (delete the layout/logs keyspace family) — a third recording of the log set with no reader must go before a split forces the question of which record wins.
title: Split CoreState from TransactionSystemLayout: make the durable/broadcast divide honest
